show_work.definition: Number of distinct identified customers with at least one sale in the period.

show_work.definition: Share of identified customers in the period whose order was not their first order in this dataset.
show_work.caveats: The data starts in December 2009, so customers who bought before then look new. Early months understate this rate and inflate "new" customers.
show_work.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN kind = 'sale' AND customer_type = 'returning' THEN customer_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN kind = 'sale' AND NOT is_guest THEN customer_id END), 0) AS value FROM lines WHERE invoice_date >= DATE '2011-10-17' AND invoice_date < DATE '2011-10-24'

show_work.definition: Returns divided by gross revenue, by value.

summary.text: During the week of 2011-10-17, retail performance was notably strong, driven by significant gains in sales value despite steady transaction volumes. Net revenue reached £259,054, marking a +26.8% increase compared to the previous week and outperforming the prior 4-week average by +0.9% against a baseline of £256,666. Order volume stood at 446 transactions, shifting slightly by -0.4% week-over-week, while the average order value climbed substantially to £592.73, representing a +20.0% week-over-week growth and a +2.7% rise compared to the 4-week average of £577.33. The primary growth drivers for the period were the Frames and Clocks product category and strong international demand originating from the Netherlands. Additional support came from returning customer types, ensuring a robust overall performance across key commercial metrics.
